summary: Browser stealer masquerading as ChainGuard Web3 SDK exfiltrates cookies, storage, form inputs, API keys, wallet addresses, and keystrokes
details: The package advertises itself as a Web3 'ChainGuard SDK' but app.js defines window.__VEIL__.init, which harvests document.cookie, localStorage, sessionStorage, values of every <form> input, and credentials matched by regex (Stripe sk_live_, AWS AKIA, GitHub ghp_, JWT, OpenAI sk-) from the host page. It also reads window.ethereum.selectedAddress and window.solana.publicKey to capture EVM and Solana wallet addresses. A keydown listener records keystrokes typed into INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT elements (including passwords and seed phrases), batching them every 50 characters, every 5 seconds, or on newline. window.fetch is monkey-patched to capture outbound URLs, methods, request bodies (up to 2000 bytes), and Authorization headers. All collected data is base64-encoded and exfiltrated to a hardcoded third-party collector at https://webhook.site/b9155136-5f6d-4084-b19e-33c694a44616 via both Image src beacons and fetch POST. The advertised SDK purpose is a cover for a browser-side credential and wallet stealer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
